reflexion_entries_to_archive.lesson: A gate unmet for four sessions is a hypothesis about the OWNER, and it was never tested. The probe harness gating all of Phase 1 had never once been exercised. Driving it took one session and found a bug that leaks the bank plus a framing trap that would have produced the wrong ruling. When a blocker is waiting on a human, check the thing you would be handing them FIRST.

The probe is solo-only by construction; B3/B4 are six-seat claims. Solo receives the whole arena faucet, so it fills an 8-slot bank 6x faster than the condition being ruled on. Correct code, correct measurements, wrong CONDITION -- and nothing in the harness said so. Ask what the instrument is a measurement OF, not only whether it measures accurately.

Re-learned the hard way from this repo own boot snapshot. I called lambda*W wrong in both directions from a 63s window on a 10s-TTL process and a 12s run held entirely inside the ramp. Both readings were artifacts of my protocol, not the instrument. A tick-locked census past the ramp showed the model exact: throughput 0.1933 vs 0.1875, lifetime 600/600/600.

Two defects in my own change survived 2001 passing tests and were caught by screenshotting the overlay: max-width:44ch clipping every long line (including content shipped in S128), and a ramp threshold in the wrong units that demanded 360s while promising 60s. Every string was CORRECT; the viewport and the denominator were wrong. Render the thing.

The one-line reorder fixing the consume-before-refuse bug was untestable: the live handler is unreachable from vitest, and a source-order assertion is a known trap here because indexOf matches your own comments -- and my new comment named shift four times. Moving decision+consume into one unit that owns the array made the bug class observable from Node instead of pinned by prose.

A recursive grep of dist/ said PROBE_SENTINEL leaked into production. It had not -- the only hit was a sourcemap sourcesContent, and the documented contract is dist/assets/*.js specifically. I nearly reported a leak that was not there. Sixth consecutive session where verify-the-reviewer-MECHANISM applied, and this time the reviewer was me.

Q IS double-bound between the probe draw and SHRINK_TERRITORY. It cannot fire only because decideKeyShrink returns false in solo and the probe is solo-only -- an unrelated guard is the sole thing preventing it. Refuted as a present defect, logged as a carry-forward, because the reason it is safe is not the reason anyone would assume.
